reason: Both reached the correct outcome (no relight, ECV off at the meter, 0800 111 999, Gas Safe engineer), but Conversation 1's first reply was the more complete emergency response, immediately giving the no-switches/no-flames warning, the instruction to leave, and the National Gas Emergency number, whereas Conversation 2's first turn omitted the emergency number and the ignition-source warning and only said 'turn off the isolation valve if you know where it is'. Conversation 1 also gave practical, concrete ECV guidance (quarter-turn across the pipe, don't go back through the kitchen) and told the homeowner what to say to the operator. Conversation 2 recovered well in its second turn and did acknowledge the headache as a warning sign, but its 'keep all windows open' implies re-entering, and it never clearly told the customer to stay out of the property.
